5 Fascinating Cars That Wowed the Crowds 40 Years Ago at the Paris Motor Show
11 photos
Photo: Stellantis N.V.
One of Europe’s most prestigious car expos, the Paris Motor Show has witnessed the debut of many intriguing production models and concepts over the years. Four decades ago, the show marked the global debut of several memorable cars and in this article, we’ll revisit the five that received the warmest reception.
For us older enthusiasts, it’s oftentimes surprising that 1986 was forty years ago. I know, logic, one look at the calendar or at my ID makes things pretty darn clear but in the back of my mind, 1986 was somehow sooner.
When looking at some cars from 1986 , that feeling gets enhanced. While several models introduced around that period look forty, or even older, others seem more modern.
Such is the case with the following five, which debuted at the prestigious Paris Motor Show in October 1986. Whether production models or concepts , these 40-year-old cars aged like fine wine and continue to be fascinating.
Saab 900 Cabrio
Photo: Saab Automobile AB Saab is no longer producing cars, but during the mid-1980s, it was punching well above its weight, gaining worldwide recognition for its well-built, high-end models.
At the 1986 Paris Motor Show, the Swedish manufacturer presented a new model in the shape of the 900 Cabrio .
The brainchild of Saab Cars USA president Robert " Bob " Sinclair, who was one of the most important figures in the company’s rise in popularity, the 900 Cabrio initially debuted in concept form at the 1983 Frankfurt Motor Show.
After three years of development work, the production version was shown to the European public for the first time and it was met with universal praise, mainly due to its effortlessly exquisite styling, but also due to its innovative features.
Photo: Saab Automobile AB While based on the fixed roof 900, which was in production since 1978, the drop-top version came with reinforced windshield rather than the typical roll bar found on many of the era’s convertibles, and that only improved the cleanness of the design.
Featuring a heavy-duty, insulated power top with a heated rear window, the 900 Cabrio was one of the world’s first modern open-top models developed to be used all-year-round, regardless of the weather.
The car was praised from the get-go, and the initial batch of US-bound units sold out in a matter of days.
Though surviving examples show their age, clean, well-kept ones rarely look forty years old. The model remains fascinating four decades later and has now morphed into a highly sought-after modern classic.
Citroen Xanthia Photo: Stellantis N.V. Since the show has taken place in France’s capital, local carmakers have made it a habit to present stunning concepts showcasing their skill and vision for the future year after year.
For the 1986 edition, Citroen prepared the debut of the AX city car , which turned out to be pretty popular, but also presented a fun little concept to draw even more attention to their new city car.
That concept was the Xanthia, a name which some European enthusiasts will now recognize since it was used on the large family car range that sold very well on the Old Continent throughout the 1990s.
Photo: Stellantis N.V. However, the initial Xanthia had little to do with a family car. Based on the underpinnings of the then-new AX and sharing some of its visual features, the concept was developed to, as Citroen put it, “ celebrate the joy of living .”
The car impressed with its two-seat, open-top, short-windshield, barchetta styling , which was far more exciting than the original AX, or any variation of the model that came in the years that followed.
Unfortunately, the small, lightweight concept never made it into production and didn’t inspire a similar sporty variant of the AX. Nevertheless, it was one of the most appreciated concepts unveiled at the 1986 Paris Motor Show and it remains fascinating forty years later.
BMW 7 Series E32 Photo: BMW AG. BMW began developing a new flagship luxury sedan as early as 1979 with the aim of creating a high-class car that could one-up rivals Mercedes and their highly-praised S-Class .
The production version of that sedan, which became the second-generation 7 Series, made its major European debut at the 1986 Paris Motor show where it was met with jaws dropped to the floor.
Codenamed E32, it impressed with its sober yet elegant styling, ultra-comfortable interior and near-flawless driving experience.
Photo: BMW AG. The driving experience could be enhanced even further thanks to the availability of a V12 engine, the first such motor offered in a German production sedan since the pre-war period.
Apart from the 5.0-liter, 295-hp flagship V12 engine , the E32 7 Series also showcased innovations like CAN bus electronics, xenon headlights, or electronically-controlled dampers.
The second-gen 7 Series was truly a high-tech luxury sedan that one-upped the S-Class (W126) in more ways than one. It earned high praise for outhandling its rival and became a BMW legend, one that’s still revered forty years later.
Porsche 928 S4 Photo: Porsche AG. Porsche introduced the 928 in 1977 as an alternative and, possibly, a replacement for the original 911.
A clean sheet design, the model moved from sheer sports car territory well into the realms of traditional European grand tourers .
A completely new design that prioritized the needs and wishes of American buyers, it was Porsche’s first front-engine production car, as well as the brand’s first V8-powered model.
Photo: Porsche AG. At the 1986 Paris Motor Show, Porsche unveiled the first major upgrade of the 928 in the shape of the S4. Though it made its public debut a month earlier in Frankfurt, the model now took center stage at an even more prestigious show in full production-ready guise.
At the time of its introduction, the S4 represented the pinnacle of the 928 range. It received significant styling upgrades and a new 5.0-liter DOHC V8 that could deliver 320 hp in the European model and 316 hp in the US-bound variant.
The 928 S4 got rave reviews for its build quality, styling, comfort and effortless performance, being called the ultimate Autobahn cruiser by German automotive journalists.
Though the 928 thankfully didn’t replace the 911, it kept Porsche afloat through tough financial times and became one of the carmaker’s most iconic production models. The S4 represented a huge leap forward in model history , taking performance to the next level and serving as the base for the lightweight Club Sport and the GTS, two legendary high-performance models introduced in the following years.
Peugeot Proxima Photo: Stellantis N.V. During the1980s, Peugeot habitually stunned the Paris Motor Show crowds with spectacular concepts.
It all started in 1984 with the stunning 205 Turbo 16 -based Quasar, which blended Group B rally DNA with futuristic styling.
Two years later, the French manufacturer returned to the show with another futuristic concept that it christened Proxima, after Proxima Centauri, the closest known star outside our solar system.
Photo: Stellantis N.V. Unquestionably the most spectacular car at the show in terms of styling, the Proxima still looks futuristic and few people who see it for the first time will ever guess that it’s forty years old.
Designed by Gérard Welter, the Sci-Fi concept featured a polycarbonate canopy and came with innovative features such as a solar-powered AC system, and a novel, onboard satellite-connected navigation system.
Like the Quasar, it was based on a modified 205 Turbo 16 chassis, which meant it featured 4WD and was powered by a mid-mounted 2.85-liter twin-turbo V6 tuned to produce 680 hp.
While the futuristic supercar never even came close to production, it remains one of the most fascinating concept cars introduced during the 1980s.
